2026-10-22: ALL THREE named verification gaps are now CLOSED or DETERMINED from primary sources (D-021, D-022, D-023). (a) The FCA National Storage Mechanism publishes a filing DATE, not a time: the published glossary defines 'Publication date' as 'The date a document/announcement was released via a Regulatory Information Service (RIS) or uploaded to the NSM', and the Investor User Guide defines 'Filing date' as a date. A time exists in the plumbing (the PIP-to-NSM schema carries a mandatory PublishingDate element, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) but binds PIPs only FROM 3 NOVEMBER 2025 under PS24/19. CONSEQUENCE: the two retrospective UK events (transition windows 2016-01-01 and 2019-01-01) CANNOT be timed at all, whatever the remaining verification; the UK stays viable for PH-1, whose window falls entirely after the regime starts. The NSM search API answered HTTP 403 on 2026-10-22, so condition (j) is UNVERIFIED, not false, and the failed retrieval is recorded as a failed retrieval. (b) The IFRS 18 instruments are pinned: EU T-A 2026-02-13 (date of endorsement; OJ publication 2026-02-16), UK T-A 2025-12-10 (UKEB formal adoption, closing the gap v1.2 left open), Saudi Arabia T-A 2024-12-26 (SOCPA adoption). v1.2 had registered the Saudi date 2026-06-30, which is the CMA's EARLY-ADOPTION decision (CMA_N_4083), not the instrument making IFRS 18 mandatory; the applied T-A follows the registered condition (2) and the conflict is written into the row's own fields. CONSEQUENCE, recorded in advance: the CMA-mandated pre-adoption impact disclosure (periods from 2026-04-01) falls INSIDE the Saudi transition window rather than before it, so Saudi Arabia has NO clean T-PRE anchor and its standing in PH-1 is an open design question to be settled before the holdout opens and never by looking at outcomes. (c) The published S-44 linguistic-distance index (Joshi and Lahiri 2015 friction index over 192 WALS features) CANNOT be reproduced exactly panel-wide: Ethnologue is licensed and versioned, the merge was manual, and Table 1 covers only the paper's 84-country 2004-2018 sample. The registered condition is therefore met and the REGISTERED FALLBACK ordinal scale is selected by the rule, with the published values kept as an external validation of the ordering. The fallback's category boundaries are still to be enumerated by dated decision before the holdout opens. The IFRS 18 events are registered in research/panel_v1.2.csv and deliberately NOT in the retrospective event calendar, because adding 2024-2026 rows would destroy that calendar's defining property (every retrospective event has T-A on or before 2017-10-31, so the chronological holdout split is empty; D-014).
